messages:
sec-scan-bot: ALERT: gitlab-ci artifact scan detected potential secret in job 'deploy-prod' for repo infra/terraform. Matched AWS_ACCESS_KEY_ID pattern in job log artifact: 'AKIA1234EXAMPLE'. Artifact URL: https://gitlab.example.com/groups/infra/-/jobs/6321/artifacts (redacted)

anita: copy — which pipeline run + job id? can we pull the exact log line?

sec-scan-bot: pipeline 8421, job id 6321, started 2026-02-28T03:12Z. snippet: ```[2026-02-28T03:12Z] INFO Using AWS credentials: access_key=AKIA1234EXAMPLE region=us-west-2```

mike: if that's a real key we need immediate containment. @ops-oncall please start key rotation and block deploys for infra/* until we confirm.

ops-oncall: on it. disabling shared runners for infra projects and adding temporary deny on project registry. creating emergency ticket INC-2026-023 in PD.

sara: which AWS principal is that access key attached to? can someone query IAM for the key id?

james: looked up the access key id in CloudTrail/Account console — it's associated with user "terraform-bot". last used 2026-02-27T22:54Z from our ci-runner ip range. activity looks like normal deploy usage; no anomalous API calls seen so far.

anita: regardless revoke now. rotate terraform-bot creds, then update Secrets Manager path /prod/terraform/creds and trigger a rolling deploy.

ops-oncall: revoked access key AKIA1234EXAMPLE at 2026-02-28T03:45Z. created replacement key and stored it in Secrets Manager in a new version. documenting action in INC-2026-023.

julie: quick comms question — do we need to notify GRC/customer security? This is infra repo logs only; no customer PII leaked, but compliance should be aware.

mike: yes, notify GRC and infra owners. I'll draft an internal notification, add sec/compliance to the PD incident, and recommend rotating similar-aged keys.

anita: next steps for containment: run a full artifact and repo scan for the last 90 days; search for AKIA fragments and other high-entropy patterns; run trufflehog and our gitlab-archive-scan. also audit artifact retention settings.

sec-scan-bot: scheduled full artifact scan job #8500 started (scope: infra/* artifacts, last 90d). ETA ~45m. will post results to this thread.

james: scan quick-find: 2 additional hits in older staging logs (artifact ids 1122, 1134). both match same key string and predate revocation. ops-oncall: please confirm revoked status (done).

sara: agreed hardening: reduce artifact retention for infra projects to 30 days, enable CI masking for env vars, and fail pipelines if unmasked AWS-like patterns are printed. add `git-secrets` to org pre-commit templates.

julie: audit/logging actions: append incident note in org audit log, enable CloudTrail alerts for new access-key creation and console/API usage from service principals, and raise retention of diffs for sensitive repos.

anita: KMS/secret manager follow-up: propose migrating terraform state encryption to a CMK (customer-managed KMS) and require Secrets Manager to use that CMK with least-privilege IAM roles. I'll open a PR with the IAM changes and a migration plan.

mike: follow-up checklist (short): 1) repo-wide secret scan + remediation owner @james 2) CI masking & push-rule changes owner @sara 3) pre-commit & git-secrets owner @sara 4) KMS/Secrets Manager migration owner @anita 5) post-incident retro owner @julie

ops-oncall: containment update at 2026-02-28T04:20Z: runners re-enabled with new creds, builds allowed only on protected branches until masking is enforced. closing active containment phase.

anita: adding final notes to INC-2026-023: root cause = plaintext credentials printed in CI logs by legacy deploy script; remediation = revoked key, new creds in Secrets Manager, CI masking & retention changes, pre-commit hooks. scheduling retro for next week.

sec-scan-bot: scan job #8500 completed. 14 matches found across artifact history (various projects). details uploaded to the incident ticket.

julie: thanks team, good catch. we'll cover the retro actions and SLA comms in the incident doc. :thumbsup:
